intro: Buying a home in Michigan involves more than finding a property with an affordable purchase price. Property tax reassessments, homeowners insurance, mortgage rates and seasonal maintenance expenses can all influence your monthly housing budget.

Our free Michigan mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly mortgage payment using your home price, down payment, interest rate and repayment period. Whether you're purchasing in Detroit, Grand Rapids, Ann Arbor, Lansing or another Michigan community, compare financing scenarios before making an offer.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Michigan?

blocks.markdown:
A $230,000 Michigan home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,103.17.

An illustrative monthly payment breakdown is shown below.
This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or HOA fees. The interest rate, taxes and insurance premiums are illustrative rather than verified statewide averages.

Michigan offers housing options across metropolitan communities, university towns, suburban developments and rural areas.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Michigan QuickFacts](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/MI/POP060220), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $231,600 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among homeowners with mortgages were $1,569, while approximately 73.2% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical figures provide useful context but should not be interpreted as current home sale prices.

Properties in Ann Arbor and popular metropolitan suburbs may have different purchase prices from homes in smaller communities or parts of northern Michigan.

When comparing properties, investigate local taxes, insurance premiums and transportation expenses alongside the advertised purchase price.

sections.heading: How to Use the Michigan Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Enter the expected purchase price of your property and your available down payment.

Select your preferred loan term and enter the annual interest rate offered by your lender.

Next, include the property's estimated annual taxes and homeowners insurance premium. Add monthly association fees and applicable private mortgage insurance.

Review the estimated monthly housing payment and adjust your inputs to compare different financing arrangements.

The amortization schedule helps you understand how your loan balance decreases over time and how much interest you could pay during the repayment period.

You can also use our national Mortgage Calculator to compare financing options in other states.

sections.heading: How Michigan Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Michigan's property tax system is particularly important for new homebuyers because the amount a seller currently pays may differ substantially from the buyer's future tax liability.

Understanding the distinction between market value, assessed value and taxable value can help prevent unexpected increases in monthly housing expenses.

### State Equalized Value

Michigan generally assesses real estate at 50% of its true cash value, subject to the applicable assessment and equalization process.

State Equalized Value, commonly abbreviated as SEV, represents the assessed value after equalization.

For example, a residential property with an estimated true cash value of $230,000 could have an SEV of approximately $115,000.

However, the property's taxable value may be lower than its SEV because of assessment limitations.

### Proposal A and taxable value uncapping

Michigan's Proposal A limits annual increases in taxable value, generally to the lower of inflation or 5%, subject to applicable adjustments such as additions and losses.

When a qualifying transfer of ownership occurs, the taxable value generally resets to the property's SEV in the following calendar year.

The [Michigan Department of Treasury's ownership transfer guidance](https://www.michigan.gov/en/taxes/property/change-ownership) explains this process, commonly called uncapping.

Certain legally exempt transfers do not trigger uncapping.

### Michigan property tax calculation example

Suppose you purchase a property for $230,000. Assume its SEV is $115,000, while the previous owner's taxable value is $80,000.

Under these assumptions, the new buyer's annual property tax increases by $980, equivalent to approximately $81.67 per month.

The actual future SEV and local millage rate may differ.

Use the state's official [Michigan Property Tax Estimator](https://www.michigan.gov/taxes/property/estimator) to investigate property taxes in your intended city or township.

### Michigan Principal Residence Exemption

The [Michigan Principal Residence Exemption](https://www.michigan.gov/taxes/property/principal), commonly known as PRE, exempts qualifying primary residences from up to 18 mills of local school operating taxes.

It does not eliminate all school-related property taxes or other local property charges.

For a qualifying home with a taxable value of $115,000, an exemption from the full 18 mills would represent potential annual savings of $2,070 compared with an otherwise identical nonexempt property subject to that levy.

Confirm eligibility and filing requirements with your local assessor.

The PRE is separate from Michigan's income-based Homestead Property Tax Credit.

Michigan homeowners may experience severe thunderstorms, hail, freezing temperatures, heavy snowfall and flooding.

Insurance premiums depend on the property's location, replacement cost, construction materials, condition and selected coverage.

Obtain multiple insurance quotes before completing your purchase.

### Flood and water backup coverage

The [Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services](https://www.michigan.gov/difs/consumers/disaster-prep/flood) explains that standard homeowners policies exclude flood damage.

Separate flood insurance may be available through the National Flood Insurance Program or private insurers.

Homeowners can also investigate endorsements that provide limited coverage for sewer or water backup damage.

Flood insurance and sewer backup coverage are different products. Purchasing one does not necessarily provide protection against the risks covered by the other.

Check the property's flood designation using the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home).

### Winter-related insurance considerations

Michigan's winter weather can create additional property maintenance requirements.

Inspect the condition of roofing, insulation, heating equipment and plumbing before purchasing a home.

Ask your insurer about coverage for frozen pipes, ice-related damage and other winter hazards. Review applicable exclusions and maintenance requirements.

Include any additional insurance premiums when estimating your monthly housing expenses.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These estimates exclude property taxes, insurance, mortgage insurance and association fees.

Use the complete Michigan mortgage calculator to compare the monthly expenses associated with individual properties.

The Michigan State Housing Development Authority, commonly known as MSHDA, offers mortgage financing and down payment assistance through approved lenders.

### MI Home Loan program

The [MI Home Loan program](https://www.michigan.gov/en/mshda/Pathway-to-Housing/mi-home-loan) serves eligible first-time buyers statewide and qualifying repeat buyers in designated targeted areas.

First-time buyers generally must not have owned a home during the preceding three years.

The published program requirements include:

- A minimum credit score of 640.
- Household income restrictions based on location and family size.
- A statewide purchase price limit of $566,355, effective after June 1, 2026.

Additional lender and property requirements apply.

### MI 10K Down Payment Assistance

The [MI 10K DPA Loan](https://www.michigan.gov/mshda/homeownership/mi-10k-dpa-loan) provides eligible borrowers with up to $10,000 toward down payment, closing costs and qualifying prepaid expenses.

The assistance is available statewide and must be combined with an eligible MSHDA MI Home Loan.

It takes the form of an interest-free deferred loan without scheduled monthly payments.

Repayment becomes due when specified events occur, such as selling or refinancing the home, paying off the primary mortgage or ceasing to occupy the property.

Borrowers must also complete approved homebuyer education.

Although the assistance can reduce your upfront cash requirements, it remains a future financial obligation rather than an unconditional grant.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Michigan Home

blocks.markdown:
Michigan homebuyers should prepare for expenses beyond their mortgage payments.

Winter heating, snow removal, roof maintenance and weather-related repairs can affect household budgets.

Older properties may require electrical, plumbing or heating system improvements.

Buyers considering rural or northern Michigan properties should also investigate private wells, septic systems and access road maintenance.

Properties used as seasonal residences may have different tax and insurance requirements from qualifying primary residences.

Request historical utility bills and arrange a professional inspection before committing to a property.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Michigan?

blocks.markdown:
Start with your reliable monthly take-home income and subtract household expenses, existing debts and savings contributions.

Use our [Michigan Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/michigan-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate income after applicable payroll deductions. Our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help you understand existing borrowing obligations.

Allow enough room for potential property tax increases following ownership transfers.

Compare lender offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

Maintain emergency savings for unexpected repairs and insurance deductibles rather than spending all available funds on the down payment.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $230,000 Michigan home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, principal and interest would be approximately $1,103.17 monthly. Taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### Do Michigan property taxes increase when you buy a house?

They can. A qualifying ownership transfer generally causes taxable value to reset to State Equalized Value in the following calendar year. This may increase your tax liability compared with the previous owner's bill.

### Does Michigan offer $10,000 in down payment assistance?

Yes. Eligible buyers may qualify for up to $10,000 through MSHDA's MI 10K DPA Loan. The assistance is an interest-free deferred loan combined with an eligible MI Home Loan, subject to program requirements.

Use our Michigan mortgage calculator to compare purchase prices, interest rates, down payments and repayment periods.

Pay particular attention to property tax estimates following an ownership transfer. Replacing illustrative expenses with accurate local taxes and insurance premiums can help you establish a sustainable homebuying budget.
